findings.detail: The new step discards a cached .git only if it has a symlink, a non-sample hook, or a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, include.* or includeIf.*. It says the restored .git "runs nothing", but the check is incomplete. Config keys such as filter.<name>.smudge/clean/process (paired with a .git/info/attributes file, which is not inspected), core.sshCommand, core.pager, core.askpass, credential.helper, diff.external, gpg.program, alias.* and uploadpack.packObjectsHook can still run commands or redirect git. The following actions/checkout and git operations read that config. A poisoned cache entry, for example one from a compromised push to master or dev, which are the only refs that save .git, could still get code execution on the runner. Fix: validate .git against an allowlist of expected config keys, or delete everything in .git/config except a minimal set (remote and core basics), and reject .git/info/attributes. Alternatively, restore only the objects and packs and regenerate config and hooks.
findings.title: Restored-.git sanitizer is a denylist; other config keys can still execute code during checkout

findings.detail: The new 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git' step (also replayed in ci-master.yml) rejects a restored .git only if it has a symlink, a non-sample hook, or a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeIf. The comment claims the restored .git 'runs nothing', but the check is incomplete. Keys such as filter.<name>.smudge/clean/process (paired with an uninspected .git/info/attributes), core.sshCommand, core.pager, core.askpass, credential.helper, diff.external, gpg.program, alias.* and uploadpack.packObjectsHook can still execute commands or redirect git when the following checkout and git steps read that config. A poisoned cache entry, for example one saved from a compromised push to master or dev, could then run code on the runner. This is residual hardening incompleteness, not a regression versus base, which only ran fsck. Fix: allowlist expected config keys, or rewrite .git/config to a minimal set, reject .git/info/attributes, or restore only objects and packs.
findings.title: Restored-.git sanitizer is a denylist; other config keys can still run code during checkout
